newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ FUTURES END LOWER AHEAD OF PRIVATE ESTIMATE.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ FUTURES END LOWER AHEAD OF PRIVATE ESTIMATE.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed lower on the day with the benchmark September contract failing to hold key 80.00 cents.

Traders said nervousness before a private estimate of the 1997/98 Florida crop may have sparked speculative selling into a buying vacuum. Citrus Consulting International will release its highly-anticipated forecast on Thursday.
"It's a little negative that we closed under 80.00 cents today but it's all meaningless until we get the nubmer out of the way, which will set the pace for the next two months," a broker said.
Industry sources pegged Thursday's estimated between 230 million and 235 million 90-lb boxes. The U.S. Department of Agriculture put this year's crop at a record 225.7 million boxes.
The USDA will issue its first estimate of the Florida crop in October.
The September contract finished 2.05 cents lower at 79.25 cents a lb, having ranged from 81.20 to 79.25 cents. The rest of the board finished 2.00 to 1.10 cents weaker.
Firm resistance remains at 83.00 cents, but analysts do not expect another test of the key level unless Thursday's estimate comes in over 235 million boxes.
Support was seen at 78.00 cents in November.
An estimated 5,000 lots changed hands compared with Tuesday's official 9,326 lots.
